title: Fixed Opposed Level Caissons and Central Rotor
description: One wholly newly authored complete fixed rotary-boat-lift-inspired display. Two complete long horizontal dry caisson shells sit at unequal heights on opposite sides of one common horizontal rotor axis. Each has an integral thick floor and two full tall sidewalls, two entire closed end-gate leaves and a short complete journal at each end. Two broad continuous profiled double-ended rotor arms connect both opposed chamber stations directly to the central axle; each arm is one whole solid, not a rim with radial spokes. Two complete grounded tapered outer piers, a whole common ground plinth and a closed side drive-case exterior complete one apparatus. The empty chambers remain level in this single fixed angled arrangement. Unlike the older inclined caisson carriage, there are no sloping rails, unequal-height wheel underframes or remote haul station. Unlike the observation wheel, there are no complete circular rims, perimeter suspension links or repeated small passenger tubs; unlike the twin-arm amusement ride, neither arm ends in a counterweight opposite one common seated tray. The new whole organization is a central opposed rotor with long gated chambers at both of its terminal axes. Every profile, chamber, arm, journal and coordinate authored anew, no older caisson, ride, wheel, gate or pier mesh imported or extracted. Four opaque constant untextured PBR appearances, metres native Z up, complete horizontal bounds-centred ground sole, one whole model zero scenes. Generic static civil-machinery artwork, not a replica of a named landmark or an engineering model. Broad rotating-lift category inspiration only. No water, boat, adjoining canal, actual rotation, gate action, gear train, level control, seal, water retention, motion envelope, balance, navigation, payload, dimensions compliance, manufacture, structural or equipment safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
